Knowing how to recognize a normal PET-CT is the basis of every reading. Physiologic distribution of FDG: brain (very intense, here excluded from the images), myocardium (variable), liver (reference for the Deauville scale), spleen, bone marrow, intestine and stomach (variable), muscles (after exertion or contraction), urinary excretion (kidneys, ureters, bladder). Every uptake must be compared with the fused CT before calling it pathologic.
In this collection the negative controls are patients studied for lymphoma, melanoma or lung cancer without FDG-avid malignant lesions on the exam.
